title: Defense-in-Depth Software Security Engineering / 2026
complexity_note: Relative expert judgment from source, not a security probability.

controls.name: Assign security ownership per service
controls.implementation: Maintain a security register with service owner, sensitive assets, access boundaries, remediation SLAs and incident contacts.
controls.acceptance: Every production service has an accountable owner and asset record.

controls.name: Asset inventory and attack surface
controls.implementation: Inventory domains, subdomains, APIs, ports, CI runners, buckets, credentials, webhooks and staging systems; reconcile against production.
controls.acceptance: Every public endpoint/port has an owner and documented business justification.
controls.tools: DNS inventory, cloud inventory, Nmap on owned assets

controls.name: STRIDE-based threat modeling
controls.implementation: Map data flows and trust boundaries for login, payments, uploads, invitations, eKYC, certificates and administration; rank misuse cases.
controls.acceptance: Every sensitive change documents at least one abuse case and its mitigation.

controls.name: ASVS and MASVS security baseline
controls.implementation: Turn risk-selected ASVS 5.0 and mobile MASVS requirements into traceable tickets and tests; select verification depth deliberately.
controls.acceptance: Each requirement has pass/fail/exception status with evidence.

controls.name: Data classification and minimization
controls.implementation: Classify public, internal, PII, identity documents, geolocation and cryptographic material; define retention and erasure.
controls.acceptance: No unneeded sensitive data persists in logs, cache, analytics or backups.

controls.name: Security SLOs and remediation windows
controls.implementation: Define organization-specific emergency handling for exploitable critical findings, short remediation for high findings and planned medium fixes.
controls.acceptance: Finding reports capture discovery, owner, due date and retest.

controls.name: High-risk change control
controls.implementation: Require second-person review for authorization, OTP, payments, certificate lifecycle, signing, CORS and server-access changes.
controls.acceptance: Ordinary developers cannot directly merge or bypass protected controls.

controls.name: Defense in depth and failure containment
controls.implementation: Protect critical flows at independent boundaries: authorization in service/query, rate limits at edge/app, secrets in vault/log redaction.
controls.acceptance: One failed ancillary control must not directly cause broad data exposure.

controls.name: Server-side authorization as the source of truth
controls.implementation: UI guards are only UX. Every controller/service and data operation must enforce role, permission and resource ownership.
controls.acceptance: User A cannot read/change B’s data by substituting an ID.
controls.tools: Nest Guards, Policy service, negative tests

controls.name: Default deny and least privilege
controls.implementation: Make newly added APIs deny by default; avoid wildcard roles, global admin assumptions and implicit permissions.
controls.acceptance: An endpoint lacking the required policy fails closed.

controls.name: Phishing-resistant authentication
controls.implementation: Prefer passkeys/WebAuthn or hardware security keys for admins and high-risk users; SMS OTP is not phishing resistant.
controls.acceptance: Admin login requires strong authentication and a secure recovery path.

controls.name: Secure web sessions and CSRF
controls.implementation: For web, favor a BFF or HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite session cookie when suitable; explicitly defend CSRF since cookies alone are insufficient.
controls.acceptance: Cross-site state changes are rejected and scripts cannot read the session cookie.

controls.name: JWT validation and refresh-token lifecycle
controls.implementation: Validate iss/aud/exp/nbf/algorithm/key; allowlist algorithms, rotate refresh tokens, store hashes server-side and detect reuse.
controls.acceptance: Reusing an old refresh token revokes the token family; logout invalidates sessions.

controls.name: Brute-force and account-enumeration defense
controls.implementation: Use combined per-IP, per-account, per-device and global budgets for login/OTP/reset; avoid revealing account existence.
controls.acceptance: Distributed guessing is contained without permanent victim lockout.

controls.name: OTP and account recovery integrity
controls.implementation: Use CSPRNG codes, short TTL, one-time atomic consume and binding to transaction/number/request; define resend invalidation policy.
controls.acceptance: Concurrent/replayed OTP submissions can succeed at most once.

controls.name: Step-up authentication for sensitive actions
controls.implementation: Require step-up authentication and audit for phone/email changes, ownership transfers, certificate revocation, payout changes and key management.
controls.acceptance: An existing session without step-up cannot complete sensitive actions.

controls.name: Concurrent sessions and revocation
controls.implementation: Provide active-device inventory, session termination, absolute and idle expiry; consider revoking others after password change.
controls.acceptance: Revoked credentials cease working within the defined revocation bound.

controls.name: Service-to-service identity
controls.implementation: Use independently scoped, short-lived credentials for internal services; never share one universal admin token.
controls.acceptance: Compromise of one service credential does not authorize unrelated services.

controls.name: Harden OAuth 2.0 / OIDC flows
controls.implementation: Use authorization code + PKCE, state/nonce, exact redirect URIs, issuer/audience checks and tight scopes; avoid implicit flow/wildcards.
controls.acceptance: Invalid state or forged redirects are rejected.

controls.name: Risk-based session controls
controls.implementation: Use notifications and step-up for abnormal login, new devices and high-value operations instead of relying on fixed-IP rules.
controls.acceptance: High-risk events are searchable without storing credentials.

controls.name: Avoid sanitizer bypasses
controls.implementation: Restrict/review bypassSecurityTrustHtml/Url and manual innerHTML; render untrusted data using Angular safe bindings.
controls.acceptance: XSS payloads do not execute in rich text, tables, popovers or URLs.

controls.name: Content Security Policy and Trusted Types
controls.implementation: Roll out restrictive CSP in Report-Only then enforce; use valid per-response nonces or autoCsp and Angular- compatible Trusted Types.
controls.acceptance: App works without unnecessary unsafe-eval/script unsafe-inline; violation reports are actionable.

controls.name: AOT production and no dynamic templates
controls.implementation: Build production with AOT; never compile runtime templates assembled from user-controlled strings.
controls.acceptance: No production code compiles untrusted templates.

controls.name: Safer browser credential storage
controls.implementation: Avoid long-lived tokens in localStorage where feasible; evaluate BFF/secure cookies or in-memory access tokens with constrained refresh.
controls.acceptance: A hypothetical XSS cannot extract refresh tokens from Web Storage.

controls.name: Frontend/backend XSRF contract
controls.implementation: Configure Angular HttpClient XSRF for the intended origin and enforce server-side validation; an interceptor alone is insufficient.
controls.acceptance: Forged state-changing requests with valid cookies but bad CSRF proof are denied.

controls.name: SSR host and proxy trust hardening
controls.implementation: Use Angular SSR host allowlists and only trusted proxy headers; ensure hydration HTML never exposes other users’ sensitive data.
controls.acceptance: Spoofed Host and shared SSR caches cannot leak another user’s HTML.

controls.name: Route guards are not authorization
controls.implementation: Treat hidden buttons, disabled controls and route guards as UX, never as security enforcement; API must independently authorize.
controls.acceptance: Bypassing frontend guards never grants additional API access.

controls.name: Third-party scripts and UI dependencies
controls.implementation: Minimize and version tag managers, analytics, map SDKs and CDN scripts; apply SRI when applicable and constrain with CSP.
controls.acceptance: No private key or unapproved PII is sent to third-party SDKs.

controls.name: Frontend upload hygiene
controls.implementation: Validate size/type in UI for UX only; enforce validation/scanning at backend and avoid unsafe previews or lasting blob URLs.
controls.acceptance: Backend rejects malicious uploads even when UI restrictions are bypassed.

controls.name: Service Worker and browser cache policy
controls.implementation: Ensure PWA, SSR and CDN never share-cache authenticated, OTP, profile or financial responses; clear private caches on logout.
controls.acceptance: Next user/offline browser cannot see prior session private data after logout.

controls.name: Safe navigation and redirects
controls.implementation: Allowlist return URLs, external links and deep-link destinations; block javascript: URLs and open redirects.
controls.acceptance: Untrusted input cannot redirect users to attacker domains.

controls.name: Production build and source-map disclosure
controls.implementation: Exclude dev servers, debug endpoints, stack traces, secrets and private environment values from bundles; control public source-map release.
controls.acceptance: Scanning built assets finds no credential or hidden admin secret.

controls.name: Map/chart tooltip and HTML content
controls.implementation: Treat site names, KPIs, legends, popups and chatbot output as untrusted in Mapbox/ECharts/Highcharts; use safe formatters.
controls.acceptance: Markup/JS supplied as data never executes in tooltips, markers or labels.

controls.name: Strict DTOs and mass-assignment prevention
controls.implementation: Apply ValidationPipe with whitelist and forbidNonWhitelisted to create/update DTOs; never persist raw request bodies as entities.
controls.acceptance: Injected role, tenantId, paid and isActive properties are rejected.

controls.name: Strict CORS without treating it as auth
controls.implementation: Allowlist exact trusted origins; only pair credentials with explicit origins; never treat CORS as an authorization control.
controls.acceptance: Untrusted origins cannot read browser responses; direct clients are still authorized.

controls.name: Security headers at edge and application
controls.implementation: Configure HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and service-appropriate CSP through Nest/Helmet and reverse proxy.
controls.acceptance: Normal and error responses carry the required headers.

controls.name: Layered rate and resource limits
controls.implementation: Use Redis-backed shared rate limits per IP/user/tenant/endpoint; apply tighter sensitive-route budgets, body limits and concurrency ceilings.
controls.acceptance: Limits remain effective across replicas and through proxies.

controls.name: JWT verification and signing-key rotation
controls.implementation: Use a vetted JWT library with algorithm allowlist; manage keys via kid and rotation and reject none/ algorithm confusion.
controls.acceptance: Bad signatures, wrong issuers and expired JWTs are rejected.

controls.name: Validate inputs and shape outputs
controls.implementation: Constrain query/body/path inputs and nested objects; response DTOs only expose authorized fields.
controls.acceptance: Responses never expose password hashes, secrets, internal notes or other-tenant data.

controls.name: Parameterized database access
controls.implementation: Parameterize ORM queries; reject interpolated raw SQL, arbitrary sort columns and untrusted NoSQL operators.
controls.acceptance: Injection probes in filters/search/sort cannot change query semantics.

controls.name: SSRF defense for fetchers and webhooks
controls.implementation: Server-side URL fetchers need scheme/host allowlists, DNS/IP checks including redirects, blocked internal/ metadata addresses and egress restrictions.
controls.acceptance: Requests to loopback, private address space and cloud metadata fail.

controls.name: Secure file upload and processing
controls.implementation: Enforce count/size, magic bytes, type allowlists, safe filenames, non-webroot storage, malware scanning and isolated PDF/image processing.
controls.acceptance: Polyglots, huge files, zip bombs and traversal cannot execute or expose data.

controls.name: Safe error handling and fail-closed behavior
controls.implementation: Use exception filters with traceable error IDs; never return stack traces, SQL, secrets or filesystem paths; fail closed on network errors.
controls.acceptance: 4xx/5xx responses disclose no internals and auth fails closed on timeouts.

controls.name: WebSocket authentication and message authorization
controls.implementation: Validate identity/origin at handshake and authorize every subscription/message to room/tenant; cap message size/rate and manage backpressure.
controls.acceptance: Tenant A never receives another tenant’s room messages.

controls.name: GraphQL depth/cost and batching limits
controls.implementation: Limit GraphQL depth, complexity, pagination and batch sizes; restrict production introspection where appropriate; authorize each resolver.
controls.acceptance: Nested queries or large batches cannot exhaust DB/CPU.

controls.name: API inventory, versions and deprecation
controls.implementation: Inventory REST/GraphQL/WS endpoints and versions; retire exposed legacy/debug routes and protect production API docs.
controls.acceptance: No deprecated, unowned endpoint remains exposed.

controls.name: Background-job and queue security
controls.implementation: Validate job payloads, bind jobs to verified user/tenant context, make retries idempotent and restrict queue administration.
controls.acceptance: Forged queued jobs cannot operate on other tenants or run admin operations.

controls.name: Trusted proxy and client-IP attribution
controls.implementation: Trust X-Forwarded-For only through known proxy hops/networks; do not allow spoofed client IPs to defeat rate limits.
controls.acceptance: An internet client cannot change its attributed IP by injecting XFF.

controls.name: Authenticate and replay-protect webhooks
controls.implementation: Verify HMAC/Ed25519 signatures over raw bodies, timestamp windows and event IDs; handle duplicates idempotently.
controls.acceptance: Forged, expired or duplicate webhooks cannot corrupt payment/issuance state.

controls.name: Object-level authorization (BOLA/IDOR)
controls.implementation: Query by both resource ID and authorized tenant/user; UUIDs are not an authorization mechanism.
controls.acceptance: Two-user/two-tenant negative tests cover GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.

controls.name: Field-level authorization / BOPLA
controls.implementation: Disallow normal users from directly editing price, roles, approval, ownerId or certificateStatus or seeing restricted response fields.
controls.acceptance: Adding privileged or unknown JSON properties has no effect.

controls.name: Context-aware permissions (RBAC + ABAC)
controls.implementation: Combine roles with context such as site, campus, tenant, owner, status and time; tenant admins never become cross-tenant admins.
controls.acceptance: Test both allowed and denied role/context combinations.

controls.name: Explicit business state machines
controls.implementation: Define allowed server-side transitions for payment, issuance, eKYC, invitation, approval and activation; never trust client step order.
controls.acceptance: Skipped steps, illegal rollback and invalid failed→issued transitions are rejected.

controls.name: Race-condition and double-submit resistance
controls.implementation: Protect coupon use, payments, issuance/revocation and booking using transactions, uniqueness, idempotency keys and appropriate locks.
controls.acceptance: Ten concurrent requests produce no more than one valid mutation.
controls.tools: DB transactions, advisory locks, load test

controls.name: Payment idempotency and settlement
controls.implementation: Treat provider-side verification and internal ledger as truth; browser return URLs or client flags do not prove payment.
controls.acceptance: Callback replay or retry never double-charges or double-issues.

controls.name: Business-flow abuse budgets
controls.implementation: Set per-user/tenant/period budgets for invitations, resends, trials, vouchers, exports, notifications and heavy reports.
controls.acceptance: One account cannot exceed intended send/credit/CPU budgets.

controls.name: File download and export authorization
controls.implementation: Authorize file, identity image and PDF downloads; issue scoped short-lived signed URLs; default objects to private.
controls.acceptance: Changing a file/export ID never reveals another user’s document.

controls.name: Invitation and account-binding controls
controls.implementation: Use expiring one-time invitations bound to recipient, tenant and role; email changes must not elevate role.
controls.acceptance: Invitation replay/tampering cannot enroll the wrong user or tenant.

controls.name: Server-authoritative pricing and discounts
controls.implementation: Compute prices, taxes, inventory and discounts server-side; never accept client cart totals as settlement authority.
controls.acceptance: Tampering with request prices cannot lower payable amount.

controls.name: Tamper-evident business audit trail
controls.implementation: Record actor, action, tenant, time and before/after metadata; separate business audit from technical logs and protect integrity.
controls.acceptance: Admin, payment and revocation history can be reconstructed.

controls.name: Ownership-transfer and privileged lifecycle
controls.implementation: Enforce dedicated policy and step-up for ownership transfer, account deletion, tenant moves and privilege changes; GET must be side-effect free.
controls.acceptance: Forged requests cannot transfer ownership to the attacker.

controls.name: Secure storage for keys and tokens
controls.implementation: Use Keychain/Android Keystore via suitable secure-storage APIs; keep long-lived secrets out of SharedPreferences and plaintext files.
controls.acceptance: Backups, adb and normal file extraction do not reveal tokens/private keys.

controls.name: TLS and platform network policy
controls.implementation: Disallow production cleartext traffic; remove accept-all TLS callbacks/debug exceptions and maintain narrow iOS ATS exceptions.
controls.acceptance: Invalid TLS certificates and disallowed HTTP requests fail.

controls.name: Risk-based certificate pinning
controls.implementation: Use pinning only where justified; include backup pins and a rotation/incident plan because incorrect rotation can brick connectivity.
controls.acceptance: Certificate rotation and emergency recovery are tested before rollout.

controls.name: Deep-link and exported-component safety
controls.implementation: Validate deep links, Intents, exported components and OTP/payment callbacks with allowlists, authorization and state.
controls.acceptance: Another app cannot trigger unauthorized signing/issuance through an Intent.

controls.name: WebView and JavaScript bridge containment
controls.implementation: Allowlist WebView origins/navigation and expose least-privileged native bridges; untrusted pages must not invoke native crypto.
controls.acceptance: An external page cannot invoke bridge methods to read data or sign.

controls.name: Server validation despite tampered clients
controls.implementation: Root/jailbreak checks and obfuscation only raise attacker cost; server must independently validate permissions and signatures.
controls.acceptance: A modified client cannot forge paid/issued server states.

controls.name: App integrity attestation signals
controls.implementation: Use Play Integrity/App Attest with fresh challenges and server verification for risky actions as supplemental risk signals; define fallback policy.
controls.acceptance: Replayed or mismatched attestations fail.

controls.name: MethodChannel and native crypto boundary
controls.implementation: Type-check MethodChannel inputs; keep native crypto capabilities narrow and do not unintentionally expose sensitive aliases/keys.
controls.acceptance: Malformed input and forged aliases cannot trigger unauthorized operations.

controls.name: Hardware-backed key handling where available
controls.implementation: Make signing keys non-exportable in Android Keystore/Keychain; assess hardware backing needs and bind generated CSRs to their actual key.
controls.acceptance: Private key never appears in Dart/HTTP/logs and CSR matches the expected public key.

controls.name: Release hardening and anti-tamper signals
controls.implementation: Ship release builds without debug flags, sensitive logs or test endpoints; use measured obfuscation without mistaking it for encryption.
controls.acceptance: Release APK/IPA contains no hardcoded secret or privileged hidden URL.

controls.name: Protect sensitive UI, screenshots and clipboard
controls.implementation: Reduce exposure of PIN/OTP/identity/certificate/key data through screenshots, app-switcher previews, clipboard and accessibility where appropriate.
controls.acceptance: Background previews and UI logs do not expose confidential data.

controls.name: Protect app signing and release distribution
controls.implementation: Restrict signing keys outside repositories, use secure CI release signing, official distribution and artifact verification/revocation plans.
controls.acceptance: Ordinary development runners cannot read production release signing keys.
controls.tools: App Store Connect, Play App Signing, CI protected env

controls.name: Offline/retry and persisted-state integrity
controls.implementation: In Flutter BLoC/AppSession, server remains authoritative for registration/certificate progress; persisted state/retries must not fabricate success.
controls.acceptance: Offline mutation/restart replay never creates fake paid/issued state.

controls.name: Minimize permissions and SDK tracking
controls.implementation: Request camera, files, location, notification permissions only as needed; strip unnecessary analytics/third- party tracking data.
controls.acceptance: Every permission has a documented feature and purpose.

controls.name: Bind each CSR to its actual key pair
controls.implementation: Maintain internal request-to-key mapping and verify CSR public key against the intended native key.
controls.acceptance: Concurrent CSRs and retries cannot cross-bind keys.

controls.name: Modern approved signing algorithms
controls.implementation: Prefer SHA-256+ with RSA/ECDSA and appropriate padding under CA requirements; avoid SHA-1 for new signatures absent a documented exception.
controls.acceptance: Clients cannot select disallowed weak signing algorithms.

controls.name: Sign canonical, bound request bytes
controls.implementation: Sign exactly the bytes transmitted, binding destination, transaction ID and validity; avoid JSON serialization drift.
controls.acceptance: Any post-signing field mutation invalidates verification.

controls.name: Explicit user consent for signing
controls.implementation: Show transaction subject/recipient/effect and bind local PIN/consent to the current operation; never permit silent signing.
controls.acceptance: WebView/background callers cannot sign without valid current consent.

controls.name: Certificate issuance/revocation invariants
controls.implementation: Server owns pending/issued/revoked/expired state; issuance/revocation must be idempotent and audited with no illegal repeats.
controls.acceptance: Repeated revoke or post-revoke issuance follows explicit reject/idempotent policy.

controls.name: Validate certificate chains and intended usage
controls.implementation: Validate issuer, chain, constraints, key usage, EKU, validity, status and subject binding when consuming certificates; Base64 presence is not proof.
controls.acceptance: Expired, revoked or wrong-EKU certificates are rejected.

controls.name: Protect issuance/signing infrastructure keys
controls.implementation: Use HSM/KMS as warranted for CA/server keys; dual control for critical operations, rotation and tested disaster recovery.
controls.acceptance: CA private keys are absent from repositories, plaintext backups and logs.

controls.name: Least-privileged database accounts
controls.implementation: Separate app, migration and backup database roles; app credentials should not be superuser or schema owner by default.
controls.acceptance: App credentials cannot create roles or read unrelated schemas.

controls.name: Tenant scopes and row-level security
controls.implementation: Tenant-scope all queries and consider PostgreSQL RLS for sensitive tables; derive tenant context from trusted identity, not request bodies.
controls.acceptance: Direct queries under app role cannot expose another tenant.

controls.name: Encryption in transit and at rest
controls.implementation: Enable TLS across untrusted service boundaries and disk encryption; consider field encryption with separate KMS keys for high-impact fields.
controls.acceptance: Stolen backup/volume media cannot be read without keys.

controls.name: Encrypted, isolated backups
controls.implementation: Encrypt and isolate backups with immutable/versioned storage; do not keep the sole backup on the application host.
controls.acceptance: Backup and keys are separated and a real restore succeeds.

controls.name: Retention and verified deletion
controls.implementation: Define retention for OTPs, sessions, audits, PII, images and exports; run scheduled deletion with documented legal exceptions.
controls.acceptance: Expired data and exports do not outlive the defined policy.

controls.name: Private object storage defaults
controls.implementation: Keep sensitive buckets private; use per-service IAM, short-lived signed URLs and safe Content-Disposition/ content-type.
controls.acceptance: Unsigned or altered object IDs do not expose files.

controls.name: Sanitize data in non-production environments
controls.implementation: Do not copy raw production data into test/staging; anonymize datasets, rotate secrets and keep test access controlled.
controls.acceptance: Staging holds no uncontrolled real PII or production tokens.

controls.name: Safe reporting, exports and analytics
controls.implementation: Allowlist export columns, paginate, cap report volume, authorize jobs and store generated artifacts privately with short TTL.
controls.acceptance: Export parameters cannot reveal restricted columns or tenants.

controls.name: Redis and queue data exposure
controls.implementation: Keep Redis/brokers on private networks with ACLs/TLS as appropriate, key namespaces and TTL; never log raw session secrets.
controls.acceptance: Internet and unrelated services cannot access the keyspace.

controls.name: OS, Node and OpenSSL patch management
controls.implementation: Run supported OS/kernel/OpenSSL/Node/proxy versions; combine KEV, severity, exploit likelihood and exposure for patch priority.
controls.acceptance: Internet-exposed exploitable critical issues meet emergency remediation SLA.
controls.tools: Unattended updates with change control, KEV

controls.name: SSH key-only and controlled admin access
controls.implementation: Disable SSH passwords and root login; place administration behind VPN/bastion with MFA and central logs where possible.
controls.acceptance: Public password/root SSH attempts fail and access grants are reviewed.

controls.name: Default-deny host/network firewall
controls.implementation: Expose only required ports; keep Postgres, Redis, metrics, SSH and Docker API off the public internet.
controls.acceptance: External scans show only explicitly approved services.

controls.name: Modern TLS configuration and HSTS
controls.implementation: Use modern supported TLS/ciphers, automate certificates with expiry alerting, and enable HSTS after checking subdomain impact.
controls.acceptance: HTTP redirects securely and TLS checks find no deprecated settings.

controls.name: Edge timeouts, body limits and connection caps
controls.implementation: Set realistic body/header size, timeouts, connection ceilings and edge limits to curb resource exhaustion.
controls.acceptance: Oversized and slow requests terminate before exhausting the app.

controls.name: WAF and volumetric DDoS protection
controls.implementation: Consider managed WAF or ModSecurity/Coraza with tuned rules, challenges and false-positive monitoring; WAF never replaces AuthZ.
controls.acceptance: Commodity attacks decrease without blocking legitimate flows.

controls.name: Separate management plane
controls.implementation: Keep GitLab administration, DB admin, metrics, Grafana, backups and SSH on private/VPN networks with SSO/MFA.
controls.acceptance: Internet cannot directly reach management panels.

controls.name: Kernel/process isolation
controls.implementation: Apply AppArmor/SELinux, non-root systemd identities, NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem and capability restrictions with compatibility tests.
controls.acceptance: Node processes cannot mutate /etc, SSH keys or other services.

controls.name: DNS, domain and certificate hygiene
controls.implementation: Protect registrars with MFA/locks, review CAA and DNS records, and monitor dangling CNAMEs/subdomain takeover.
controls.acceptance: No DNS record points to an unclaimed retired service.

controls.name: Restrict admin/debug/metrics endpoints
controls.implementation: A basic health probe may be public, but detailed health, metrics, profiler, Swagger and debug consoles require auth/network restrictions.
controls.acceptance: Unauthenticated clients cannot retrieve secrets, dumps or topology.

controls.name: Resilience, quotas and emergency isolation
controls.implementation: Limit CPU/memory/file descriptors/workers and API costs; practice emergency feature kill switches and rollbacks.
controls.acceptance: One abused service does not take down the entire host and DB.

controls.name: Non-root, reduced-capability containers
controls.implementation: Use non-root USER, read-only root filesystems where compatible, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges and bounded tmpfs.
controls.acceptance: Containers cannot escalate to host root or write arbitrary filesystem paths.

controls.name: No privileged containers or Docker socket mounts
controls.implementation: Disallow privileged containers and /var/run/docker.sock mounts; use constrained intermediary services where Docker control is necessary.
controls.acceptance: No internet-facing container can control the Docker daemon.

controls.name: Micro-segmentation and egress
controls.implementation: Isolate edge, backend, DB and brokers; allow only needed flows and restrict workload egress to metadata/ management networks.
controls.acceptance: Web containers cannot directly reach DB or unrelated services.

controls.name: Minimal trusted container images
controls.implementation: Use minimal supported and digest-pinned base images, separate builder/runtime stages and scan final artifacts.
controls.acceptance: Production images lack unnecessary compilers and fixable exploitable critical CVEs.

controls.name: Runtime secrets rather than image layers
controls.implementation: Keep secrets out of Dockerfile layers, committed Compose files, image ENV and startup logs; use secret mounts/vault with rotation.
controls.acceptance: Image layers/history and artifacts do not reveal enduring secrets.
controls.tools: Vault, cloud secret manager, CI protected vars

controls.name: Cloud IAM least privilege
controls.implementation: Use per-workload identities limited by actions/resources; avoid broad administrator roles and embedded static cloud keys.
controls.acceptance: Image service cannot read backup buckets or unrelated KMS keys.

controls.name: Kubernetes hardening (if applicable)
controls.implementation: If running K8s, enforce restricted pods, seccomp, non-root, resource quotas, network policies and disabled token auto-mount where unneeded.
controls.acceptance: Ordinary pods cannot gain cluster/other-namespace admin access.

controls.name: Infrastructure-as-code policy scanning
controls.implementation: Scan Terraform/Compose/Helm/cloud config pre-merge for public buckets, open ports, secrets and wildcard IAM.
controls.acceptance: Critical misconfiguration rules fail a merge pipeline.

controls.name: Environment and key separation
controls.implementation: Separate production and dev/test accounts, networks, databases, secrets and runners; test credentials cannot mutate production.
controls.acceptance: Development credentials are rejected by production.

controls.name: Ingress trust chain and TLS termination
controls.implementation: Constrain trusted proxy chains, re-encrypt/mTLS internally when warranted and enforce host allowlists; do not trust internet-supplied forwarding.
controls.acceptance: Host/XFF spoofing cannot alter recovery links or rate attribution.

controls.name: Protected branches and mandatory review
controls.implementation: Protect main/release, require second approval for sensitive paths, use CODEOWNERS and restrict force/ direct pushes; audit emergency overrides.
controls.acceptance: Developers cannot change production releases without approval.

controls.name: Isolated and short-lived CI runners
controls.implementation: Avoid shared privileged runners with production secrets; prefer dedicated ephemeral runners for sensitive pipelines and isolate caches.
controls.acceptance: Untrusted merge requests cannot access protected secrets or production runners.

controls.name: Secret detection and verified rotation
controls.implementation: Run pre-commit/pipeline secret scanning and periodic history checks; revoke exposed secrets immediately since deleting commits is insufficient.
controls.acceptance: Seeded test secrets fail the gate; leaked real secrets are revoked.

controls.name: SAST for TypeScript, Dart and native code
controls.implementation: Use Semgrep/CodeQL where supported plus custom rules for AuthZ, innerHTML, raw SQL, HTTP and bridges; tune false positives.
controls.acceptance: A seeded vulnerable PR is detected by the intended rule.
controls.tools: Semgrep, GitLab SAST, custom rule tests

controls.name: Dependency vulnerability management
controls.implementation: Use lockfiles, advisory monitoring, regular upgrades and gates for genuinely exploitable findings across npm, pub, Gradle and CocoaPods.
controls.acceptance: Unwaived exploitable critical dependencies cannot ship.

controls.name: Software bill of materials (SBOM)
controls.implementation: Generate CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM per app/image release and monitor it post-release against evolving CVE intelligence.
controls.acceptance: Every release has a versioned SBOM with documented exceptions.

controls.name: Artifact signing and build provenance
controls.implementation: Sign images/artifacts and generate verifiable provenance; assess isolated builds against SLSA 1.2.
controls.acceptance: Deploy accepts only approved signed artifacts/provenance.

controls.name: Pin CI actions/images and restrict pipeline scripts
controls.implementation: Pin CI tool images and downloaded scripts to vetted versions/digests; avoid unreviewed curl-pipe-shell.
controls.acceptance: Upstream changes cannot silently alter runner-executed code.

controls.name: Controlled deployment, approvals and rollback
controls.implementation: Use protected production environments, approvals for risky deploys, immutable artifacts and rehearsed rollback.
controls.acceptance: Every production change maps to an authorized, logged job.

controls.name: Authenticated DAST in owned staging
controls.implementation: Run ZAP automation against owned staging OpenAPI and authenticated flows using low-privilege test accounts; plan active production scans carefully.
controls.acceptance: True findings get remediation and false positives are documented.
controls.tools: OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite for review

controls.name: Container and IaC release gates
controls.implementation: Run Trivy/Checkov on merge and release artifacts; combine severity, exploitability and expiry-bound waivers.
controls.acceptance: No unwaived exploitable critical image issue ships.

controls.name: Security invariants in automated tests
controls.implementation: Automate negative and concurrent tests for AuthZ, OTP, IDOR, payments, state transitions and tenant isolation; gate merges.
controls.acceptance: Every sensitive feature has at least one high-risk negative test.

controls.name: AI-generated code and dependency provenance
controls.implementation: Require human review, tests and secret scanning for agent code; verify existence, publisher, version and necessity of suggested packages.
controls.acceptance: Agents cannot silently change secrets, CI permissions or admin routes.

controls.name: Time-bound security exceptions
controls.implementation: Track each false-positive/accepted-risk waiver with owner, expiry, rationale and compensating controls.
controls.acceptance: Expired waivers re-open or alert automatically.

controls.name: Structured, redacted security logs
controls.implementation: Log userId/tenantId/traceId/event/result; redact JWTs, OTPs, passwords, sensitive CSRs, PII and private keys.
controls.acceptance: Log review finds no full tokens or PINs.

controls.name: Actionable detection rules
controls.implementation: Alert on spikes in 401/403, OTP failures, role changes, heavy exports, invalid webhooks and unusual admin logins.
controls.acceptance: Synthetic security alerts reach on-call with a runbook.

controls.name: Off-host immutable-ish log retention
controls.implementation: Ship security events off host quickly, restrict delete access and synchronize clocks across systems.
controls.acceptance: An app-level compromise cannot wipe central audit trails.

controls.name: Incident-response runbooks and tabletop
controls.implementation: Rehearse token leaks, RCE, ransomware, CA failure and data breaches with isolate/rotate/evidence/notify/ restore steps.
controls.acceptance: Exercises establish decision owners and measured recovery times.

controls.name: Tested backups and measured RPO/RTO
controls.implementation: Set service RPO/RTO and periodically restore DB, object store, secrets and configuration into a separate environment.
controls.acceptance: Restore and integrity are demonstrated, not inferred from backup success.

controls.name: Continuous external exposure monitoring
controls.implementation: Monitor changes in DNS, ports, certificates, artifacts, leaked repos and public buckets on authorized assets.
controls.acceptance: Unexpected DB-port exposure raises an alert within SLA.

controls.name: Vulnerability intelligence and KEV triage
controls.implementation: Correlate CISA KEV and framework/runtime advisories with asset inventory/SBOM; prioritize by exposure.
controls.acceptance: Applicable CVEs receive owner and due date within SLA.

controls.name: Security contact and vulnerability disclosure
controls.implementation: Publish security.txt/contact, vulnerability scope, intake, triage, coordinated fixes and an appropriate safe- harbor policy.
controls.acceptance: A test report is acknowledged and triaged within stated windows.

controls.name: Measurable security outcomes
controls.implementation: Measure critical remediation time, AuthZ negative-test coverage, secret scanning, patch latency, restore success and detection latency.
controls.acceptance: Monthly metrics link to underlying CI and incident evidence.

controls.name: Multi-identity BOLA regression tests
controls.implementation: Maintain A/B users, A/B tenants, admin and guest fixtures; run cross-identity object-ID probes via integration tests.
controls.acceptance: No unauthorized cross-user reads/writes succeed.

controls.name: Workflow and business logic abuse tests
controls.implementation: Exercise skipped stages, replay, duplicate submission, state tampering, price changes, invitation reuse, tenant switch and concurrency.
controls.acceptance: Each valuable workflow has security invariants and negative cases.

controls.name: Authenticated web/API DAST
controls.implementation: Run staging DAST with guest/user/admin sessions plus OpenAPI; anonymous-only scanning misses many authorization bugs.
controls.acceptance: Findings include endpoint, identity and reproducible evidence.

controls.name: Mobile security verification with MASVS/MASTG
controls.implementation: Assess release APK/IPA with MobSF plus manual storage, WebView, keychain/keystore, TLS, URL scheme and tamper tests.
controls.acceptance: MASVS findings have evidence and remediation ownership.
controls.tools: MobSF, MASTG, Frida in authorized lab

controls.name: Staged bug bounty program
controls.implementation: Start with private VDP/bounty after the baseline; define scope, testing limits, SLAs and reward rules before considering public launch.
controls.acceptance: Triage can reliably reproduce IDOR, SSRF and RCE reports.

controls.name: Retest, root cause and regression gate
controls.implementation: After remediation, document root cause and add a negative CI regression; fixing one URL instance is not enough.
controls.acceptance: Previously failing exploit fixtures stay blocked.

controls.name: HTTP protocol and misconfiguration checks
controls.implementation: Review request smuggling, host headers, cache poisoning, path normalization, CORS and SSRF within approved test scope.
controls.acceptance: Proxy/backend parsing and host trust have no exploitable discrepancy.

controls.name: Targeted fuzzing and property-based testing
controls.implementation: Fuzz CSV/PDF/JSON parsers, uploads, deep links, GraphQL and signing serializers with bounded resources.
controls.acceptance: Inputs do not trigger reproducible crashes, unbounded work or signing mismatch.

controls.name: Authorization after role/tenant changes
controls.implementation: After role downgrade, revoke, logout or tenant switch, probe stale sessions and cached tokens against the authorization matrix.
controls.acceptance: Old privileges do not persist through stale caches or tokens.

controls.name: Independent review before sensitive launches
controls.implementation: Obtain independent security review or scoped penetration testing before launching payment, PKI, identity- data or high-exposure APIs.
controls.acceptance: Exploitable critical/high findings trigger remediation or documented no-go.
